source.ref: fixed by 13ddd46 (#163), from the second 2026-09-27 audit (F2, F3, F4)

rationale: The first version of /ocra override took write access from author_association, bound to a 7-character commit prefix, and credited edited comments to their original author. People without write access, a ground commit or an edit could each pass a blocking verdict. ADR-0036: kept.

expect.concern: Write access comes from author_association, but MEMBER is any organization member and COLLABORATOR can be read-only, so people without write access can override a blocking verdict.
The override binds to a commit prefix of as few as 7 hex characters (28 bits), so an author can grind a new commit with the same prefix and carry an old override onto changed code.

An override is credited to the comment's original author even when someone else edited it, so a pull request author with write access can edit a maintainer's old comment into /ocra override and pass their own change.
